title: Runtime compatibility covenant: semantic version policy, LTS channels, and gated rollouts
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Establish a pragmatic semantic versioning policy and associated rollout gates for the serving runtime that balances forward progress (performance and security improvements) with minimizing customer regressions. This ticket defines the policy decisions, LTS channel cadence, metadata headers for deprecations, telemetry signals to drive rollouts, and the upgrade tooling required to accelerate safe migrations. Scope: runtime public API (network and SDK surface), on-disk KV cache formats, model-serving wire contracts, and admin control-plane APIs. Excludes: internal build tooling and developer-only experimental flags. Motivation: Recent incidents where minor changes caused subtle behavior shifts in embeddings and function-calling highlighted the need for stronger compatibility semantics and automated migration aids. The policy should enable: - Clear breakage semantics for users (what requires coordination) - Fast rollback and mitigation paths for bad releases - Instrumentation to detect regressions early in canaries - Developer ergonomics for landing non-breaking and breaking work
acceptance_criteria: A single-page policy document describing what constitutes major/minor/patch changes for the runtime and examples for each
LTS channel cadence defined (schedule + supported window) and published in release calendar
A rollout gate checklist implemented in CI and the console that covers automated tests, telemetry smoke, and canary traffic routing
A minimal 'rwmigrate' CLI and migration-check API that can run compatibility checks against a customer config and report required actions
Deprecation headers and structured response metadata (X-Runtime-Deprecation, X-Runtime-Compat-Tags) implemented in runtime 2.0 alpha
decisions: Adopt semver for public runtime artifacts: MAJOR.minor.patch. MAJOR bumps for incompatible wire or persisted-format changes; minor for additive behavior and opt-in features; patch for bug fixes and non-behavioral changes
Define an LTS channel with a 12-month active support window, 18-month critical fixes window; new LTS every 12 months
All breaking changes require a documented migration path, a migration tool or shim, and a two-stage rollout (canary -> staged -> general) with automated rollback triggers
Introduce a compatibility marker in responses: "X-Runtime-Compat-Version" and deprecation warnings via "X-Runtime-Deprecation" with RFC-style dates
Require a Compatibility Impact Assessment (CIA) PR template on GitHub for any changes touching public APIs, storage formats, or the KV cache schema
rollout_gates: Gate: Unit/Integration coverage for compatibility assertions (new tests must include backward/forward compatibility checks)
Gate: Canary metrics baseline (error rate, 95/99 latency, token-level perplexity drift for generated text) within configured thresholds
Gate: Telemetry health (no regression signals from compatibility telemetry streams for 48h) before scaling canary
Gate: Customer opt-in check for changes that modify persisted formats (must have migration window and data-backup plan)
Gate: Release notes and migration guide published and linked in the release artifact
upgrade_tooling: rwmigrate CLI (alpha): validates local config and model files for migration compatibility and emits a checklist
compat-check API endpoint: POST manifest -> returns allowed upgrade path and detected incompatible items
automatic compatibility shim: lightweight server-side adapter to translate legacy wire-contracts to new contract where feasible
canary-manager integration: declarative canary groups with percentage ramp, automatic rollback on SLA breach, and automatic rollback notices to the console
migration-telemetry library: instrumentation helpers to tag requests with migration-stage and collect drift signals (client and server SDKs)
migration-runbook templates and GH PR template to capture CIA (Compatibility Impact Assessment) and migration commands
migration_examples: Breaking change example: KV cache binary layout change -> MAJOR bump. Required steps: publish conversion tool, release major with compatibility shim for 6 months, notify customers via console and X-Runtime-Deprecation header
Deprecation example: Deprecated parameter 'max_tokens' behavior change -> minor bump with response header warning for 90 days before removal; provide SDK alias automatically mapping to new param
Wire ABI change example: New structured output envelope for function-calling -> minor bump only if old envelope remains supported behind a feature flag; otherwise MAJOR with staged rollout
Performance-only change example: Kernel reorder that improves latency but is transparent to callers -> patch release unless it changes floating-point determinism affecting model outputs, then minor
telemetry_and_metrics: Baseline signals: per-route error rate, 95/99 latency, token-level output similarity (embed similarity/prompt+response drift) compared against historical baseline
Compatibility telemetry tag: 'compat_version' emitted with every request and stored in trace logs
Alerting rules: >3x baseline error-rate for 5m OR 10% drift in embedding population similarity triggers automated rollback
Experimentation metric: A/B quality delta using holdout prompt-set; require <2% quality regression or documented mitigation
Retention: compatibility traces retained for 90 days for migration forensics

notes: Trade-off: Longer LTS windows increase support burden but reduce customer upgrade churn. We chose 12/18 months as a compromise; re-evaluate after two LTS cycles.
Follow-ups: implement compatibility telemetry in SDKs (JS/Python/Go), wire up canary-manager in console, and create migration workshops for top 10 enterprise customers.
Risk: Binary on-disk format changes are high risk for Dedicated/Private installs; require additional offline tooling and clear opt-in by admins before upgrades
